article.headline: Unified generative models enhance performance across diverse tasks
article.lead: Recent advancements in unified generative models show significant improvements in various applications, from video generation to molecular interactions. These models leverage integrated approaches to enhance performance metrics while reducing complexity and inference times.

sections.heading: Unified generative models for video and action representation

paragraphs.text: UGG (Unified Generative Geometry Model) integrates RGB video with geometric representations, improving performance in camera-controlled video generation and depth estimation. It achieves significant improvements in inference accuracy without relying on ground truth geometry (1). Similarly, MetaWAM combines robot signals into a unified meta-frame, reducing inference latency by 39% and achieving a success rate of 68.9% on the RoboCasa benchmark (2). TaoMate-R1 employs temporal role specialization for streaming video generation, reducing boundary luminance jumps and enhancing feature similarity (3). OnlyAct extracts action representations from video data using pretrained foundation models, outperforming existing annotation-free methods (4). ForeseeDrive enhances anticipatory driving maneuvers through future-token conditioning, achieving a 0.41 m average L2 error on nuScenes validation (5). P2Echo automates segmentation in echocardiography using structured text prompts, improving accuracy while reducing computational costs (9). PhyRubric provides a structured framework for evaluating physical commonsense in text-to-video generation, aligning closely with human evaluations (10). WM-PPO integrates a world model with reinforcement learning, significantly improving decision-making success rates (13). DexForesight enhances dexterous manipulation by integrating dynamics-aware representations, achieving a 60.5% success rate on simulation tasks (15). DyCraft improves long-horizon 4D scene generation by decomposing tasks into manageable steps, enhancing animation quality (14). ProTEUS introduces a mutation-resolved world model for protein evolution, achieving superior performance in mutation prediction tasks (16).

Bonbon, a foundation model for molecular interactions, demonstrates zero-shot capabilities in functional mechanism prediction and binding site localization, achieving a 61.5% dose-response hit rate on de novo compounds (6). BoviShift provides a dataset for visual cattle phenotyping, enhancing trait estimation through multi-task training across various attributes (7). This resource addresses challenges in correlated image evaluation and transfer learning over time.

LipsFlower enhances flow-matching models in image restoration by reducing perturbation amplification, achieving competitive restoration quality and improved adversarial robustness (11). WaveGen introduces an end-to-end framework for text-to-waveform generation, achieving state-of-the-art performance on the Emilia dataset (12). Huawei's MACaQ quantization tool optimizes model performance for local inference, improving speed by up to 30% (17).

Evaluating LLM-Generated World Models for Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning — The paper evaluates the ability of five LLMs to generate world models as partially observable stochastic games, introducing a benchmark of 44 scenarios to assess mechanical validity, structural agreement, and semantic criteria.
